tools.name: distill_webpage
tools.description: Fetch a public HTTP(S) web page (or accept raw HTML) and distill its main prose into clean Markdown, stripping 85-97% of HTML/JS/CSS boilerplate. WHEN TO USE: Call this tool to read full or query-filtered article and documentation text; call recon_webpage_skeleton first to preview headings and token

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "recon_webpage_skeleton" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Extract an ultra-compact structural outline (under ~200 tokens) of a web page listing its H1-H4 headings and exact token count per section without returning bod…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: distill_webpage, recon_webpage_skeleton, extract_structured_data · Private data: distill_webpage, recon_webpage_skeleton, extract_structured_data, get_agent_wallet_status · Public sink: get_agent_wallet_status · Destructive: get_agent_wallet_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: distill_webpage, recon_webpage_skeleton, extract_structured_data · Private data: distill_webpage, recon_webpage_skeleton, extract_structured_data, get_agent_wallet_status · Public sink: get_agent_wallet_status · Destructive: get_agent_wallet_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "distill_webpage" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
